title: Grade 7
blurb: Unit-by-unit practice for the whole Grade 7 year — proportional relationships, rational-number operations, equations and inequalities, percent applications, scale and circles, probability, and sampling.

units.title: Proportional Relationships
units.blurb: Unit rates with fractions, the constant of proportionality, recognising proportionality, and solving proportions.

units.title: Rational Number Operations
units.blurb: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing signed fractions and decimals, and placing them on the number line.

units.title: Equations & Inequalities
units.blurb: Two-step equations, rational coefficients, writing equations from stories, and solving inequalities.

units.title: Percent Applications
units.blurb: The percent equation, multipliers, markup, discount and tax, simple interest and percent error.

units.title: Geometry: Scale, Angles & Circles
units.blurb: Scale drawings, angle relationships, the triangle inequality, circumference, area of circles and composite figures.

units.title: Probability
units.blurb: Simple probability, complements, sample spaces, theoretical against experimental, and compound events.

units.title: Sampling & Statistics
units.blurb: Populations and samples, bias, inference, mean, median with outliers, range and mean absolute deviation.

forms.title: Proportional or not?
forms.skill: Every pair must give the same quotient, not just increase together.

variants.statement: A table pairs $x = 2, 4, 7$ with $y = 4, 8, 14$. Is the relationship proportional?
options: Yes — every $y \div x$ is the same
No — the ratios $y \div x$ are not all equal
It cannot be decided from three pairs
variants.explanation: Each pair gives $y \div x = 2$, so it is proportional.
